concepts.name: Origin and Course of the Mahanadi River
key_dimensions: Origin near Sihawa in Chhattisgarh (NOT Odisha — a common UPSC trap)
States traversed: Chhattisgarh and Odisha only
Drains into Bay of Bengal near Cuttack via a large delta
Comparison with other rivers originating in Central Indian highlands

concepts.name: Origin and Course of the Godavari River
key_dimensions: Longest peninsular river — originates at Trimbakeshwar, Nashik (Western Ghats)
Flows through Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh before meeting Bay of Bengal
Known as 'Dakshin Ganga' or 'Vridha Ganga' — significance of this title
Comparison with Krishna in terms of basin area and discharge

concepts.name: Origin and Course of the Krishna River
key_dimensions: Originates at Mahabaleshwar in Western Ghats (Maharashtra)
Flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh
Joins Bay of Bengal near Hamasaladeevi — not near a major city (trap point)
Major tributaries: Tungabhadra, Bhima, Musi, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha

concepts.name: Origin and Course of the Kaveri River
key_dimensions: Originates at Talakaveri in Brahmagiri Hills, Coorg (Karnataka)
Flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu — only two states (trap: not Kerala)
Forms Sivasamudram Island and falls — Asia's second largest waterfall by flow
Drains into Bay of Bengal near Poompuhar; sacred status as 'Dakshin Ganga' of South

concepts.name: Delta Formation by East-Flowing Peninsular Rivers
key_dimensions: Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri all form significant deltas — contrast with west-flowing rivers that form estuaries
Godavari and Krishna deltas form a combined mega-delta in Andhra Pradesh
Kaveri delta — known as 'granary of South India'; fertile rice bowl
Reason east-flowing rivers form deltas: gentle gradient near coast, high sediment load

concepts.name: Drainage Basin Area Hierarchy of East-Flowing Peninsular Rivers
key_dimensions: Correct order: Godavari > Krishna > Mahanadi > Kaveri (frequently tested in ranking questions)
Godavari has the largest basin among all peninsular rivers
Kaveri has the smallest basin among the four major east-flowing rivers
UPSC trap: confusing discharge with basin area rankings

concepts.name: Tributaries of the Godavari River
key_dimensions: Major tributaries: Pravara, Manjra, Wardha, Wainganga, Penganga (left bank); Indravati, Sabari, Sileru (right bank)
Indravati — important right-bank tributary originating in Odisha; Chitrakote Falls on it
Wardha-Wainganga system — often confused as separate rivers but merge before joining Godavari
Pranhita = Wardha + Wainganga + Penganga combined: largest tributary of Godavari

concepts.name: Tributaries of the Krishna River
key_dimensions: Tungabhadra — most important tributary; itself formed by Tunga + Bhadra rivers
Bhima originates near Bhimashankar (Western Ghats) — flows through Solapur
Musi River passes through Hyderabad — important for river pollution context
Left-bank tributaries (Bhima, Musi) vs right-bank tributaries (Tungabhadra, Ghataprabha)

concepts.name: Tributaries of the Mahanadi River
key_dimensions: Major tributaries: Seonath, Jonk, Hasdeo, Mand, Ib (left bank); Tel, Ong (right bank)
Tel River — largest tributary of Mahanadi; originates in Eastern Ghats
Hasdeo River — coal-rich region; environmental controversy (Hasdeo Arand forests)
Hirakud Dam built on Mahanadi near Sambalpur — one of longest earthen dams in world

concepts.name: Tributaries of the Kaveri River
key_dimensions: Major tributaries: Hemavati, Shimsha, Arkavathi (left bank from Karnataka)
Kabini, Bhavani, Noyyal, Amaravati (right bank from Kerala and Tamil Nadu)
Kabini originates in Kerala — important for Kaveri water dispute interstate angle
Mettur Dam (Stanley Reservoir) on Kaveri in Tamil Nadu — significance for irrigation

concepts.name: Inter-State Water Disputes of East-Flowing Rivers
key_dimensions: Kaveri Water Dispute: Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Puducherry — Kaveri Water Disputes Tribunal (1990), final award 2007, Supreme Court modification 2018
Mahanadi Water Dispute: Chhattisgarh vs Odisha — Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal constituted 2018
Krishna Water Disputes: Bachawat Tribunal (1969) and Brijesh Kumar Tribunal (2010)
Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal (1969) — allocated water among Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha

concepts.name: Major Dams and Reservoirs on East-Flowing Peninsular Rivers
key_dimensions: Hirakud Dam (Mahanadi) — world's longest dam; Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam on Krishna
Almatti Dam on Krishna (Karnataka) — source of dispute with Andhra Pradesh
Polavaram Project on Godavari — national project status; inter-state controversy
Mettur Dam on Kaveri — one of India's oldest large dams; agrarian significance in Tamil Nadu

concepts.name: West-Flowing vs East-Flowing Peninsular Rivers: Structural Contrast
key_dimensions: East-flowing rivers have longer courses, gentler gradients, form deltas (west-flowing form estuaries)
Western Ghats act as the main watershed — rivers on eastern slope are longer than western slope rivers
East-flowing rivers receive both southwest and northeast monsoon — Kaveri unique in receiving NE monsoon significantly
West-flowing rivers (Narmada, Tapi) flow through rift valleys — east-flowing rivers do not (important trap)

concepts.name: Kaveri River and the Northeast Monsoon Significance
key_dimensions: Kaveri is unique among peninsular rivers — its upper catchment gets SW monsoon, lower Tamil Nadu delta gets NE monsoon
Ensures perennial or near-perennial flow — important for Karnataka-Tamil Nadu dispute
This dual monsoon dependence is the core reason Tamil Nadu argues for guaranteed flows in dry months
Contrast with Godavari and Krishna which are more SW monsoon dependent

concepts.name: Waterfalls Associated with East-Flowing Peninsular Rivers
key_dimensions: Chitrakote Falls on Indravati (Godavari tributary) — widest waterfall in India ('Niagara of India')
Sivasamudram Falls on Kaveri — first hydroelectric project of India set up here (1902)
Dhuandhar Falls on Narmada (trap: Narmada is west-flowing, not east — do not confuse)
Barehipani and Joranda Falls in Odisha near Mahanadi basin — located in Simlipal

concepts.name: Godavari River: Sacred, Cultural, and Environmental Significance
key_dimensions: Kumbh Mela held at Nashik on Godavari (Sinhastha Kumbh) every 12 years
Papikonda National Park located along Godavari gorge in Andhra Pradesh
Mangrove ecosystems and estuarine biodiversity in Godavari delta — Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary
Polavaram Dam — designated national project; submergence of tribal areas and displacement issues

concepts.name: River Linking Projects Involving East-Flowing Peninsular Rivers
key_dimensions: Ken-Betwa Link Project — though Ken is a Yamuna tributary, peninsular river-linking context
Godavari-Krishna link — Polavaram-Vijayawada link already operational in parts
Mahanadi-Godavari-Krishna-Kaveri link — part of National River Linking Project (Peninsular Component)
Controversies: ecological impacts, inter-state consent issues, displacement of communities

concepts.name: Minor East-Flowing Peninsular Rivers: Pennar, Palar, Vaigai
key_dimensions: Pennar (Pinakini) originates in Nandi Hills, Karnataka — flows through Andhra Pradesh into Bay of Bengal
Palar originates in Karnataka, flows through Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh — inter-state basin
Vaigai originates in Varushanad Hills (Tamil Nadu) — flows through Madurai; largely seasonal
These rivers are often ignored but appear in options as distractors or in match-the-following questions

concepts.name: Eastern Ghats and Their Influence on East-Flowing Rivers
key_dimensions: Eastern Ghats are discontinuous — rivers like Mahanadi, Godavari cut through them forming gorges
Papikonda gorge (Godavari), Borra Caves region — Eastern Ghats' geomorphic influence
Eastern Ghats do not act as a major watershed unlike Western Ghats — rivers rise before reaching them
Erosional features: the rivers have young valleys in Eastern Ghats sections despite overall old age

concepts.name: Comparison: Himalayan Rivers vs East-Flowing Peninsular Rivers
key_dimensions: Peninsular rivers are rain-fed and seasonal (except Kaveri which is near-perennial); Himalayan rivers are perennial due to snowmelt
Peninsular rivers have fixed and stable courses; Himalayan rivers are still eroding and shifting
Peninsular rivers flow over hard crystalline rock — less sediment; Himalayan rivers carry more silt
UPSC trap: Godavari is sometimes called perennial — clarify it is largely rain-fed but has large storage
